content.user_title: Build Azure Cosmos DB TypeScript Workflows
content.value_statement: Azure Cosmos DB data operations can be hard to implement correctly in TypeScript. This skill gives focused SDK guidance for CRUD, queries, bulk writes, partition keys, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install @azure/cosmos and @azure/identity for Node.js projects.
Explains CosmosClient setup with DefaultAzureCredential, account keys, or connection strings.
Provides CRUD examples for creating, reading, replacing, upserting, patching, and deleting documents.
Covers simple queries, parameterized queries, pagination, and cross-partition query options.
Documents bulk operations and simple or hierarchical partition key usage.
Includes error handling patterns for common Cosmos DB status codes and ETag concurrency.
limitations: It covers the data plane SDK, not Azure Resource Manager account provisioning.
Examples require a valid Azure Cosmos DB account, database, container, and credentials.
It does not execute migrations, deploy infrastructure, or verify live account permissions.
Generated code still needs project-specific tests, retries, and security review.

use_cases.title: Create a TypeScript data layer
use_cases.description: Design typed services that read and write Cosmos DB documents with clear partition key handling.

use_cases.title: Improve Cosmos DB query safety
use_cases.description: Convert ad hoc query examples into parameterized SDK calls with pagination and cross-partition guidance.

use_cases.title: Handle operational errors
use_cases.description: Add handling for missing documents, conflicts, rate limits, ETags, and retry-aware service behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to configure a CosmosClient in TypeScript. Use DefaultAzureCredential and environment variables for account settings.

prompt_templates.title: Create CRUD Methods
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a TypeScript service for products in Cosmos DB. Include create, read by id, replace, upsert, patch, and delete flows.

prompt_templates.title: Build Safe Queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write parameterized Cosmos DB queries with pagination. Explain when cross-partition queries are appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Cosmos DB data access design. Focus on partition keys, bulk operations, 429 handling, ETags, and credential choices.

output_examples.input: I need a Cosmos DB service for product documents in TypeScript.
output_examples.output: A service outline with client setup, typed document methods, partition key usage, and error handling notes.

output_examples.input: My query filters by category and price from user input.
output_examples.output: A safer query plan using named parameters, page size guidance, and notes about cross-partition cost.

output_examples.input: I need to update many documents and avoid lost updates.
output_examples.output: A bulk operation approach with ETag checks, conflict handling, and rate limit retry considerations.

best_practices: Prefer Microsoft Entra authentication with DefaultAzureCredential when the environment supports it.
Use parameterized queries and explicit partition keys to improve safety, cost, and performance.
Handle 404, 409, 412, and 429 responses as normal operational cases.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode account keys or connection strings in application source files.
Do not use cross-partition queries by default when a partition key can be supplied.
Do not treat sample code as production ready without retries, telemetry, and tests.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure Cosmos DB accounts?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the @azure/cosmos data plane SDK for documents, queries, containers, and related operations.

faq.question: Which languages does it target?
faq.answer: It targets JavaScript and TypeScript projects that use the Azure Cosmos DB SDK for Node.js.

faq.question: Does it support Microsoft Entra authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends DefaultAzureCredential and also documents key-based options for environments that require them.

faq.question: Can it help with partition key design?
faq.answer: It explains simple and hierarchical partition key usage, but final design depends on workload access patterns.

faq.question: Does it include query guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers simple queries, parameterized queries, pagination, and cross-partition query behavior.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible workflows.
